title: Continuing with Evidence: Certificates, Acquisition Costs, and Human Effort in Agent Memory
abstract: A memory system may retain a correction without making it available for the next justified action, or shift thereconstruction of evidence to its user. We study these failures through an engineering case and a finite modelof evidence-carrying continuation. The model separates acquired observations from the certificate delivered toa verifier, and terminal packet bytes from machine and human acquisition costs. Its applicability depends on anadequate contract already available or constructed as explicitly accounted preparation work; the proceduredoes not itself remove that burden. We instantiate established decision-region determination, certificatesufficiency, and Pareto dynamic programming, proving soundness and completeness within a fixed finitepolicy class. A predictable observation can reduce the delivered certificate after a decision is already known. Areference implementation checks 2,744 contracts and agrees with unpruned enumeration on 36 smallercontracts. A subsequent ablation finds changed frontiers in 48 of the 2,744 contracts when predictable queriesare forbidden. A distinct audit of 1,525 archived records identifies 16 erroneous source exclusions andsubstantial complete-bundle delivery constraints. The associated prospective user study was closed before anynatural case because its input requirements did not fit the intended work. The contribution is a reproducibleacquisition/export contract, exact witnesses and a bounded engineering audit. These results establishconditional guarantees, not improved natural collaboration; preparing the contract remains part of theapplicability question.

title: Variance-Optimal Control Variates for Learning with Black-box Feedback
abstract: Modern models increasingly learn through black-box oracles such as humans, optimization solvers, and external tools that provide feedback without exposing their internal mechanisms. A common remedy is to learn an (action-)value function as a control variate. In this paper, we first observe that even an exact action-value function can be arbitrarily far from variance-optimal. We show that this gap arises because the value function minimizes the noise in each action's own gradient term, while an action can still affect the rest of the gradient estimator through shared parameters. A simple unbiased correction, at no extra oracle cost, can still reduce its variance by an arbitrarily large factor. Motivated by this, we then prove that the residual variance can be decomposed exactly by actions with no cross terms. This decomposition yields a closed-form variance-minimizing correction for neural-network parameters, which can be computed by a simple projection. Empirically, our correction consistently reduces the variance left by the value function and improves learning across all tasks. The source code for all experiments is available at https://github.com/Zihao-Kevin/black_box_opt.

title: gatecall: what may leave the company, and where it may go
abstract: gatecall is a Claude Code plugin that keeps a company's data on its routes. Its hooks stop a message, a command, a web request or a tool call that carries an API key or token, a payment card number (Luhn-checked), an IBAN (ISO 13616 mod-97), a national ID number with its check digit, or a list of people's e-mail addresses or phone numbers, and say why in the person's language. Red folders are read only by a model on the company's own computer. Profiles cover any company, the EU and US defence contractors (no DeepSeek model, API or weights); program rules keep other AI agents (kimi, grok, agy) to training folders, cleaned copies and no blanket permissions. It writes a permissions.deny block with absolute paths and keeps a journal of kinds and rules that holds each stopped value only as a fingerprint under the company's own key (HMAC-SHA256) or as a count, with a retention period and an export. Python standard library only, no network.

title: Psycho-Social Pressure and Measurement Architecture — BIT Dual-Track Terminal Synthesis
abstract: English abstract Terminal synthesis of two completed Boundary Information Theory psycho-social research tracks: (A) theoretical/synthetic psycho-social pressure, typed state transfer and abstract multi-agent dynamics; (B) domain semantics, executable measurement architecture and synthetic measurement/identification robustness. The release preserves negative results H2-05 and M2-09, scale and causal-identification firewalls, and a frontier seed ledger. title: A Realistic Multi-Platform Social Media Threat Dataset – Public Release
abstract: This dataset provides a cleaned and deduplicated collection of English-language social media posts designed for research on social media threat detection and classification. It supports binary threat detection and multiclass analysis of cybersecurity-related content across multiple social media platforms. The public release includes the main dataset, a data dictionary, a README file, and checksum information for integrity verification. This dataset is associated with the publication:Yasir A. Matnee and Saad Albawi, “A realistic multi-platform social media threat dataset,” IET Conference Proceedings, 2025. DOI: 10.1049/icp.2025.4375. Researchers using this dataset are requested to cite both the Zenodo dataset record and the associated publication.

title: Repeated-Measure Leakage, Distribution Shift, and Reliability under Partial Observation in Patient World Models
abstract: Patient world models are increasingly proposed for longitudinal prediction, intervention-aware reasoning, and clinical-trial simulation. Causal or clinical intervention validity is distinct from predictive generalization and reliability; before making stronger claims, the underlying predictive state should generalize across patients, survive realistic shifts and missing observations, and expose failure through meaningful reliability signals. We evaluate these prerequisites in a deliberately narrow setting: short-horizon digital-biomarker forecasting from PhysioNet GaitPDB, comprising 165 participants, 306 recordings, and 51,129 context-future pairs. Using persistence, ridge, MLP, GRU, Transformer, and a compact JEPA-style predictor, we build an evaluation ladder that progressively removes raw temporal overlap, same-recording familiarity, and same-patient familiarity before testing unseen-patient generalization. For GRU, NMSE rises from 0.1227 under random-window splitting to 0.1393 after eliminating raw train-test overlap and to 0.1961 under patient holdout. Among 54 participants with repeated recordings, exposure to a different recording from the same patient improves GRU NMSE from 0.2177 to 0.1556, while a recording-excluded identity hypothesis is not supported at the participant level. Under participant-held-out evaluation, MLP and Transformer are statistically indistinguishable. Study shift, a four-times-longer prediction gap, and partial observation further degrade performance; under 50% temporal masking, Transformer NMSE rises to 0.611 while MC-dropout predictive variance falls. We do not claim a longitudinal or intervention-aware simulator. Instead, the results support a prerequisite evaluation stack of patient separation, repeated-measure controls, shift, missingness, and uncertainty validation before stronger patient-world-model claims are trusted.

title: Exact distances and measurement allocation for logical Pauli readout
abstract: The minimum fault weight of a logical readout depends jointly on data-error persistence, check redundancy and time-boundary constraints. For any binary check matrix $H$ and nonzero parity support $w$, we prove that a repeated-readout model with a zero-syndrome endpoint has exact distance $\min_{w\cdot y=1}[\operatorname{wt}(y)+q\operatorname{wt}(Hy)]$ for at least $q$ wrong readouts. This reduces the search over fault histories to one weighted spatial minimum and gives the minimum repetition count for each adjacent-column check in square Bacon--Shor and generalized Shor readouts. Combining those checks with redundant Gauss-check pair products yields an exact joint distance and an outcome-count optimum within the specified gauged-readout family. At target distance $m$, one round uses $m^2$ outcomes, compared with $m(2m-1)$ for the repeated baseline in the same phenomenological model. For a one-epoch bare-ancilla CNOT implementation, we prove a schedule-dependent distance upper bound by constructing an accepted wrong readout from one gate fault and outcome flips. The bound identifies necessary timing conditions for retaining the target distance and gives matching upper bounds of three for the best tested schedules at both $m=3$ and $m=5$.

title: WSI Feature
abstract: This dataset contains pre-extracted feature representations prepared for the ECE1512 course assignment. The features are provided to allow students to develop and evaluate machine-learning models without requiring direct processing of large whole-slide images (WSIs) or running computationally expensive feature extraction pipelines.

title: Attestable Audit: Property-Based Attestation for Proprietary Workloads without Artifact Disclosure
abstract: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) prove the integrity of code and data to a remote peer through remote attestation: the TEE issues an attestation report by signing, with a hardware-bound key, its configuration information, including measurements (cryptographic digests) of the code loaded inside it. A verifier appraises the report by matching these measurements against reference values. When the measured artifact is proprietary, however, the verifier cannot derive the reference values itself: it can only confirm that something with a given measurement is running inside the TEE---not that the program behaves as expected---forcing full trust in the reference value provider. We propose an architecture that closes this gap without disclosing the artifact, composing two TEE workloads: attestable build (Hugenroth et al., 2025), which binds a source code digest to a build artifact measurement, and attestable audit (proposed in this paper), which binds the same source code digest to the verdicts of automated audits---fuzzing, static analysis, AI code auditing, formal methods---executed inside a TEE. Both are instances of Confidential Computing Proofs: TEE attestation viewed as a hardware-backed zero-knowledge proof. Chaining the two certificates lets the verifier conclude that the running artifact was built from source code satisfying the audited properties, without disclosing either the source code or the build artifact. A proof-of-concept implementation on Intel SGX with the Gramine Library OS, running the Bandit security analyzer on Python code, demonstrates the practicality of the approach.

title: Language Model Fingerprinting Requires Rethinking Watermark Teachers
abstract: LLM fingerprinting via watermark distillation embeds a statistical watermark signal into model weights, enabling model owners to identify their models behind black-box APIs. Revisiting a recent protocol, we find that its utility evaluation understates text quality degradation in open-ended generation, favoring overly strong watermark teachers. Weakening the watermark improves text quality but sacrifices detectability. To move beyond this trade-off, we rethink whether text watermarks designed for verifying generated text are suitable distillation teachers for model fingerprinting. Such watermarks are typically designed to remain detectable from an individual output, limiting how sparse the watermark signal can be. In contrast, fingerprint verification can aggregate signal across queries, making sparser watermark signals viable. This raises a key question: where should the sparse signal be placed? We analyze signal placement through token surprisal and show that, even at comparable watermark strength, different placements can target tokens with different plausibility under the base model. This motivates near-tie restriction, which uses top-1-relative logit gaps to restrict the watermark bias to tokens close to the base model's top prediction. Across multiple models, near-tie improves detection--quality frontiers under deployment changes, preserves higher text quality across query budgets, and further improves existing watermarking schemes when combined with them.
